subject: Post-call: Parcellytics product team discovery & SLA roadmap
messages:
From: Tom Keller <tkeller@parcellytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ava Peterson <ava.peterson@parcellytics.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Aug 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap & constraints from today (latency / concurrency)

Hey Marissa —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Short recap from our side so we have aligned expectations before the next call.

Pain points we confirmed on the call:
- Interactive suggestions UX is frequently >2s p95 (web client) which kills discovery conversion.
- Long-running prompt completions (summaries) occasionally spike to 6-8s because our current batcher queues at high concurrency.
- We need stable streaming behavior (progressive tokens) — users see janky increments when responses are buffered then flushed.

Current stack notes:
- Frontend: React app, pragmatic SSE-based streaming pipeline.
- API: Node service (K8s) that fans out to an internal model-service using Triton-backed GPU nodes and a small CPU fallback fleet.
- Model endpoints: we run a mix of 13B open models (quantized) and a few hosted vendor endpoints for certain tasks.

Targets & success criteria (raw):
- p95 for short completion / suggestion flows: <= 500ms (goal) / <= 800ms (minimum acceptable).
- Sustained throughput target: 750–1,000 req/s for suggestions with median payload size ~120 tokens.
- Concurrent live sessions (streams): up to 500 concurrent streams during peak.

Immediate asks from Parcellytics:
1) Can Redwood run a short PoC that demonstrates streaming p95 improvement and stable multiplexing across 200 concurrent streams?
2) What instrumentation/log access do you need to help correlate spikes to batching windows?
3) Budget/contract framing: we have purchasing windows in September — would like an estimate for a 4-week PoC and longer-term reserved capacity pricing.

Attaching our internal SLA spreadsheet so you can see more detailed constraints (will share formally after this email).

Tom
Tom Keller
Head of Search Products | Parcellytics
(attachment: parcellytics-sla-reqs.xlsx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: RE: Quick recap & constraints from today (latency / concurrency)

Tom —

Appreciate the clear summary. Confirming the key takeaways and proposing next steps so everyone's aligned.

Confirmed pain points (short):
- p95 spikes on short suggestions and inconsistent streaming increments.
- Queueing at high concurrency causing tail latency for longer completions.

Proposed immediate plan (PoC scope):
1) 2-week technical PoC: validate streaming p95 for suggestions at 200 concurrent streams and 750 req/s. Deliverable: per-route p50/p95/p99 and token-level latency waterfall.
2) Instrumentation handoff: we will provide a small agent and a logging guide for request traces (no sensitive payloads). We need a set of representative prompt flows from your side (3–5).
3) Test matrix: short suggestions (avg 120 tokens), mid completions (400–800 tokens), long summaries (~2k tokens).
4) Ramp plan: start with synthetic traffic (day 0–2) then move to shadow traffic on production for 48 hours, followed by a live A/B window.

Owners & timings:
- Redwood PoC lead (technical): Rishi Malhotra — coordinate infra & test harness (owner: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com).
- Commercial/contract: me — pricing and scope, will follow up with a PoC SOW and costs (owner: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com).
- Parcellytics action: please share representative prompts and a small sampling of production latency traces (anonymized) by EOD Wed, Aug 4.

Attachments: I attached a short PoC outline we typically use — covers test scenarios, success criteria, and runbook tasks.

If that looks good, Rishi and I can do the technical kickoff on Wed (Aug 4) or Thu (Aug 5). What works for your engineers?

Thanks — looking forward.

—

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Keller <tkeller@parcellytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap & constraints from today (latency / concurrency)

Marissa / Tom —

Thanks for the context. A couple of short technical notes so the PoC can be scoped tightly: we will keep this high-level until we see traces/prompts.

On streaming UX:
- SSE vs WebSocket: SSE is fine for most browsers but has a single-connection heuristic that can cause buffering at proxies; we usually recommend a WebSocket test if clients suffer intermediate proxies.
- Progressive flush size: small token deltas (2–6 tokens) are lower-latency for perception but increase per-token overhead — we'll tune to balance p95 vs token-rate.

On batching & concurrency:
- We need to instrument the batch window duration and the average tokens-per-request to map batching efficiency to observed p95. Small batches (few requests) reduce latency but increase GPU cost.
- For your target (750 req/s, 200 concurrent streams), we'll simulate both independent short requests and multiplexed-long requests. Goal is to keep the short-suggestion p95 under 800ms during multiplexed load.

Required artifacts from Parcellytics for day 0:
1) 3 canonical suggestion prompts + expected token lengths.
2) One anonymized trace showing a ~95th percentile spike (JSON with timestamps).
3) Confirmation which endpoint currently routes to Triton vs CPU fallback.

Technical kickoff options: Wed Aug 4 10:00–11:00 PDT or Thu Aug 5 09:00–10:00 PDT. I recommend Wed so we can get initial infra spun up.

I'll prepare a short test harness (k6 + a lightweight stream replayer) and a result dashboard (Grafana snapshot) for the PoC.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
